LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 2.3.1 FICTION: NOVEL FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: why is style important in writing of a novel? 2. how do novels influence promotion of values in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner interprets and makes inference while exploring

characters and their traits while drawing lessons from them.

● Learning to learn: This is nurtured as the learner relates their learning experiences to real life when linking the

characters and language use to real life concerns and draw moral lessons.
